source_text: Ἀντεστρατήγει δὲ ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τοὺς μὲν ἀσθενεῖς ἐρρύετο, ἀντιπαρέτασσε δὲ στύλους ἑδραίους δυναμένους διὰ τῆς ὑπομονῆς πᾶσαν τὴν ὁρμὴν τοῦ πονηροῦ εἰς ἑαυτοὺς ἑλκύσαι, οἳ καὶ ὁμόσε ἐχώρουν, πᾶν εἶδος ὀνειδισμοῦ καὶ κολάσεως ἀνεχόμενοι, οἳ καὶ τὰ πολλὰ ὀλίγα ἡγούμενοι ἔσπευδον πρὸς Χριστόν, ὄντως ἐπιδεικνύμενοι ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς.
thought_title: Grace sets firm pillars to take the attack
orientation: The churches are explaining how the grace of God answered after the devil trained the pagans to shut Christians out of public life.
pass_a_gloss: But the grace of God acted as opposing general, and on the one hand it rescued the weak, and on the other it drew up in opposing line firm pillars able through endurance to draw to themselves all the attack of the evil one, who also went to close combat, enduring every kind of insult and torture, who also counting the many sufferings as small hurried toward Christ, truly showing that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy toward the coming glory to be revealed to us.

choices.why: military verb answering the devil falling upon with all strength in prior section
keeps distinct masculine singular, not the brief devil term for antikείμενος
keeps negation and comparison force toward coming glory

bible_refs.note: οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς

pass_b_english: But God's grace took the field against him like an opposing general. It rescued the weak and set firm pillars in his path, men able through endurance to draw the whole attack of the evil one onto themselves. They too closed with him in hand-to-hand combat, bearing every kind of insult and torture. They counted their many pains as small and hastened toward Christ, truly showing that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be set against the glory to come that shall be revealed in us (Romans 8:18).
